done.why: The Carousel Room scrambled my moves and the glass maze below it was hard to map, so I stopped making progress. I had not found the pearls, the stone door, the carousel's works or a use for the unicorn's key.

about: A Zork II style trip through the Great Underground Empire. A cranky Wizard pops in and casts spells on you, and the treasures he took lie south of the ravine. The map includes a formal garden with a unicorn, a disorienting carousel, a dragon, a ruined bank with a vault, and a glass maze.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, hinted at where the treasures are, and made me drop the lamp.
The carousel scrambled my directions, so I could not tell where I was going.
The Wizard's Fantasize spell put a fake gold ingot and jewels in rooms, and the world explained it was an illusion.
Room exits did not match the descriptions. Several moves put me back in the room I had just left.
The glass maze of identical rooms was impossible to map.

wished: A way to see the exits of a room.
A way to map the carousel and the glass maze.
To reach the unicorn's key and the pearls.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It gave me a goal and a direction.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: It was a funny way to explain a spell's illusion.

fun.why: The Wizard's spells and the setting were fun. The scrambling carousel and the maze wore me down.

engagement.why: There was plenty to see, but I got no real traction on the puzzles.

difficulty.why: Disorienting movement and a maze, with no obvious leads.

interestingness.why: A varied map with the Wizard's recurring spells and a real treasure hunt.

prose.why: Witty additions to the classic text, such as the Wizard's glances and the room embarrassed by the illusion.
